sections.h2: Where do Levy County owners pay and question property tax?
sections.html:
Levy County property tax is paid to the Tax Collector, whose main office is at 310 School Street, Suite 102, in Bronson (352-486-5172), with branches in Williston and Chiefland. The Property Appraiser is a separate office at 310 School Street in Bronson, reached at (352) 486-5222.

  • Bronson main office: 310 School Street, Suite 102, Bronson, FL 32621, Monday to Friday, opening 8:30 and closing 4:30
  • Williston branch: 551 SW 1st Avenue, Williston, FL 32696, (352) 528-6091.
  • Chiefland branch: 226 North Main Street, Chiefland, FL 32626, (352) 493-4646.

The Tax Collector says it cannot process address changes on real property or tangible accounts. Those go to the Property Appraiser. That includes the mailing address a seller should update so a late bill reaches the right person after a closing.

sections.h2: What are the Levy County property tax dates?
sections.html:
Real estate tax becomes due November 1 and is delinquent if unpaid by April 1 of the following year. Florida's early-payment discount runs 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February.

No later than April 30 the Tax Collector mails reminder notices on unpaid accounts, and in May it prepares a delinquent list to be advertised in a newspaper and online. The office says the tax certificate auction normally takes place on or before May 31, and the process must start on or before June 1 under Chapter 197.

Florida's annual cycle upstream of the bill is also fixed: value is set as of January 1, exemption applications are due March 1, the proposed-tax notice arrives in August, and a value petition is due within 25 days of that notice.

sections.h2: How can you pay Levy County property tax online, and what does it cost?
sections.html:
Online payment by card costs a fee that goes to the processor, while e-check online is free. The Tax Collector lists a 2.3 percent charge on credit cards, a flat $1.75 on transactions under $76, and no fee for an online e-check (ACH).

Payments made in the office are charged 2.3 percent regardless of amount, and e-checks are not available in the office. A payment processed after 11:59 p.m. is treated as received the next calendar day, which matters near a deadline. For a seller wanting a clean payoff before closing, an online e-check done before midnight avoids both the fee and the next-day rule.

Cards accepted are Visa, Master Card, American Express and Discover. Call 352-486-5172 on a weekday if the system gives trouble.

sections.h2: What happens when Levy County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax is sold as a tax certificate, which is a lien and not a transfer of the house. The certificate face amount adds the unpaid tax, interest of 1.5 percent a month for April and May, a 5 percent Tax Collector commission, the newspaper advertising charge and the tax sale cost.

Levy County tax certificate terms, from the Tax Collector's tax sale page
ItemAs the office prints it
Sale methodOnline auction through West Florida Business Systems, on or before May 31
Bid range0 to 18 percent in 0.25 percent steps, lowest rate wins
Minimum interest if redeemed on or after June 15 percent (not for zero bids)
Unbid certificatesIssued to the county at 18 percent
Certificate life7 years
Holder may seek a tax deedAfter two years from April 1 of the issuance year

The delinquent list is advertised once a week for three consecutive weeks before the sale. A holder may not contact the owner until two years have passed from April 1 of the issuance year.

sections.h2: What does a Levy County tax deed application involve?
sections.html:
The applicant submits a signed application, redeems any other outstanding certificates, pays current tax if due, and pays a $150 title search fee and a $75 application fee, which the office notes can change without notice. The Clerk of the Circuit Court then sets the sale and bills the advertising, mailing and sheriff costs.

For property with homestead on the current roll, the opening bid includes one half of the assessed value on top of the taxes and costs. A property that draws no bidder can be placed on the list of lands available for taxes, and land not bought from that list within 3 years reverts to Levy County. Government liens survive a tax deed under s. 197.552.

For an owner thinking of selling, the practical point is timing. Ask the Tax Collector for a current payoff figure on any certificate before you list, because a buyer's title company will want every lien on the parcel cleared or paid at closing.

sections.h2: What should Levy County sellers know about agricultural classification?
sections.html:
Agricultural classification does not follow the land to a new owner. The Property Appraiser's page says the classification is not transferable, so a buyer must file a new application when the property sells or transfers.

The deadline is March 1 each year, and the filing period runs from January 1 to March 1. Florida law cited by the office limits the classification to land used primarily for bona fide agricultural purposes, meaning good-faith commercial agricultural use. Agricultural zoning alone does not earn it, and the use must be in place on the January 1 assessment date or a reasonable effort made to put it in use.

If you sell acreage in Levy County, tell the buyer which parcels have the classification today, because the assessment can jump to market value if the new owner does not qualify. A denied application is mailed to the owner, who may ask to discuss it with the appraiser.

sections.h2: What does Levy County look like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Levy County is a rural county of about 48,520 people (Census Bureau estimate, July 1, 2025), up 13.1 percent from the April 2020 base, spread across 1,118 square miles, or about 38 residents per square mile in 2020.

The Census Bureau reports 22,192 housing units, an 81.4 percent owner-occupied rate, a median owner-occupied value of $190,600, median gross rent of $850 and median household income of $56,750 for 2020 to 2024. Some 26.7 percent of residents are 65 or older, and 91.1 percent of residents had not moved in the previous year. Long ownership and low turnover mean many Levy County owners have a Save Our Homes assessment well below market value, which resets on sale.

Florida deed document stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration in Levy County, collected by the clerk at recording, with all parties to the deed liable.

faqs.q: Where is the Levy County Tax Collector?
faqs.a: The main office is at 310 School Street, Suite 102, Bronson, with branches at 551 SW 1st Avenue in Williston and 226 North Main Street in Chiefland. Doors are open on weekdays.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to pay Levy County property tax online?
faqs.a: Cards carry a 2.3 percent fee, or a flat $1.75 on charges under $76, paid to the processor. An online e-check has no fee. Office payments are charged 2.3 percent.

faqs.q: When does Levy County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1 of the year after it is billed. Reminder notices go out by April 30, and the tax certificate sale normally takes place on or before May 31.

faqs.q: Can a buyer keep my Levy County agricultural classification?
faqs.a: No. The appraiser says classification is not transferable, so the buyer must file a new application by March 1 and qualify under the bona fide agriculture test.

faqs.q: How soon can a tax deed be sought on unpaid Levy County tax?
faqs.a: A certificate holder may apply after two years from April 1 of the year the certificate was issued. Ask the Tax Collector for a payoff figure if a certificate exists on your parcel.
